response: Yes, endothelin-1 (ET-1) is believed to play a role in the hemodynamic changes that occur during hemodialysis. ET-1 is a potent vasoconstrictor that can contribute to increased blood pressure and vascular resistance. During hemodialysis, the removal of fluid and electrolytes can lead to changes in blood volume and blood pressure, which can stimulate the release of ET-1. Elevated ET-1 levels have been associated with hypotension, cramping, and other hemodynamic complications that can occur during hemodialysis. Additionally, some studies suggest that ET-1 may contribute to the development of vascular access stenosis and other cardiovascular complications in patients undergoing hemodialysis. Overall, the role of ET-1 in hemodynamic changes during hemodialysis is an area of ongoing research, but it is clear that ET-1 can have significant effects on blood pressure and vascular function in this patient population.
